papers.title: OpenESM: Energy-Steered Models Are Scalable Foundation Learners
papers.problem: Text models that only guess the next word cannot search for better answers before they write.
papers.fix: Energy-steered models refine a hidden state first, then write words, and beat GPT models on most of 26 tasks.
papers.practicalUseCase: If this holds, a model can think before it writes; try the released weights before paying for a bigger model.
papers.limitation: The paper compares against GPT models only and gives no cost or speed numbers.

papers.title: SO-101 Bench: Accessible Spatial Manipulation
papers.problem: Cheap robot arms had no test that checks if they can follow spoken placement orders.
papers.fix: The best trained robot policies score near 61%, but an AI agent that writes code scores 83.2%.
papers.practicalUseCase: Your choice of agent wrapper and language model matters more than the robot policy, so tune those first.
papers.limitation: Simulation overstates success compared with the real arm, though it keeps the same ranking of policies.

papers.title: Ψ-0.6: Adaptive Streams of Thought in a Unified Vision-Language World Model
papers.problem: AI models for physical scenes use separate tools for seeing, language and shape, so they work poorly together.
papers.fix: One model mixes images, text and shape data while reasoning, and beats leading open models on spatial questions.
papers.practicalUseCase: If this holds, one model can answer 'will this fit' questions, so test spatial tasks with intermediate shape steps.
papers.limitation: The excerpt gives no exact scores, so the size of the gain is unclear.

papers.title: ParetoRSI-Gym: Can AI Agents Improve Language Models Across Multiple Domains?
papers.problem: Tests of self-improving AI agents check one score, so they miss losses in other subjects.
papers.fix: The best agent, Claude Code with Opus-5, raises scores 9.2% across five subjects, and up to 63% in one.
papers.practicalUseCase: Agent tooling matters as much as the model, so judge agents by gains across many domains, not one score.
papers.limitation: The best result came from one agent setup, and the test fixes the training method and tools.

papers.title: Sustainability Committees and Environmental Initiatives: Insights from Dual Banking Systems in Emerging Markets
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Banks set up sustainability committees, but no one knew if Islamic banks gain the same results as conventional banks.
papers.fix: Committees raise environmental scores in both bank types, but Islamic banks show gains mainly in overall scores and resource reduction.
papers.practicalUseCase: A committee alone may give Islamic banks symbolic gains, so check for real green products and innovations.
papers.limitation: The study shows links in emerging-market banks, not proof that committees cause the results.

papers.title: Trends and Determinants of Sustainability Sukuk Issuance: Evidence from Global Markets
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Little is known about how sustainability sukuk issuance grows or what sets the size of each issue.
papers.fix: Across 11,944 sukuk issues from 2012 to 2022, equity-based contracts, strong security and USD or Euro currency give larger issues.
papers.practicalUseCase: Issuers who want bigger sustainability sukuk should use equity-based contracts and strong security, and watch opinion costs.
papers.limitation: The data stops at 2022 and shows links between features and issue size, not cause.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence and Big Data Strategies to Enhance Islamic Banks’ Competitiveness and Sustainable Development
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Islamic banks in Jordan lacked proof that AI and big data help them compete and grow sustainably.
papers.fix: AI, big data and data management link to better competitiveness and sustainability; staff digital skill links only to competitiveness.
papers.practicalUseCase: Invest in AI, data tools and data management first, not only staff training, if you want sustainable results.
papers.limitation: The survey covers 214 managers at Jordanian Islamic banks at one time, so it shows links, not cause.

papers.title: ICT, High-Tech Exports, and Institutions as Drivers of Bank Expansion Growth in a Dual Banking System
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Nobody had compared what drives growth in Islamic and conventional banks across countries.
papers.fix: Across 218 banks in 12 countries, ICT use drives growth most, and high-tech exports help only with ICT.
papers.practicalUseCase: If this holds, digital investment beats other levers for bank growth, so back digital tools before other bets.
papers.limitation: The study covers 12 countries from 2010 to 2023, so results may differ elsewhere.

papers.title: Determinants of Financial Inclusion in the OIC and OECD Countries: Are They Different?
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.institution: International Centre for Education in Islamic Finance
papers.problem: Many people in Muslim-majority countries still lack formal financial services despite fast growth in Islamic finance.
papers.fix: In OIC countries, income, tertiary education, institution quality, internet access, population and age dependency shape financial inclusion.
papers.practicalUseCase: OIC countries need to invest in digital networks, youth and women empowerment, and income to reach more people.
papers.limitation: The study covers 35 countries from 2005 to 2021 and shows links, not proof of cause.

papers.title: Global prevalence of impostor phenomenon in medical students: A systematic review and meta-analysis
papers.institution: National University Toribio Rodríguez de Mendoza
papers.problem: Medical students face constant exams and comparison, but no one knew how often they feel like frauds.
papers.fix: Feeling like a fraud is common among medical students before they qualify, but estimates vary a lot between studies.
papers.practicalUseCase: If you feel like a fraud in training, know it is common, and seek support early.
papers.limitation: Results differed greatly between studies, so the pooled rate is only a rough guide.

papers.title: Exploring the influencing factors of academic doctoral students’ academic innovation behavior in the context of generative artificial intelligence: Self-determination theory and motivation-opportunity-ability perspectives
papers.problem: Doctoral students use generative AI, but it was unclear what drives their new research ideas.
papers.fix: Inner drive and outside rewards both push doctoral students to innovate, while long unmet needs cut willingness to explore.
papers.practicalUseCase: Meet your basic needs and mix curiosity with outside goals, because unmet needs block new ideas.
papers.limitation: The data comes from one-time self-reports, so it cannot prove cause or direction.
